thread:
jen: Hey team — AcmeCorp reports intermittent 403s immediately after SSO redirect when calling our Dedicated endpoint behind their L7. Works fine against hosted. They say it happens only when requests go through their edge that rewrites upstream path. Error in our logs: `invalid_session_signature` from auth middleware. Can reproduce internally but only when passing through their proxy (we have a repro L7 config).

vikram: Thanks — do we have example request/response (Set-Cookie + subsequent request) that shows the cookie value and attributes? Also what proxy tech are they using (nginx/HAProxy/Envoy/Istio)?

jen: They're on NGINX (k8s ingress). Quick repro from their side attached in support ticket: they set `proxy_cookie_path / /app/;` because the customer app is served under `/app`. They claim sometimes the API request carries the cookie, sometimes not. Our auth logs show the cookie arrives but signature verification fails. Error log snippet: `auth: cookie signature mismatch; expected hmac=abc123 got hmac=ab ` (truncated).

sam: Hmm. Two distinct possibilities: 1) cookie is being mutated by the proxy when rewriting Path (nginx `proxy_cookie_path` can rewrite `Path=` attributes on Set-Cookie), and some SSO signers include attributes in the signature (rare but possible). 2) the cookie value is being truncated/rewritten because of header encoding changes or because multiple Set-Cookie headers are being collapsed incorrectly. Need to see raw bytes.

jen: I got them to run a curl reproducer. Posting the minimal steps they used:

```bash
# fetch SSO redirect and capture cookie
curl -c cookies.txt -v 'https://auth.acme.example/sso?redirect=https://edge.acme.example/app/login'
# follow redirect -> client ends up with cookie set by our auth service (Name=ACMESESS)

# call the protected API behind their L7
curl -b cookies.txt -v 'https://edge.acme.example/app/api/v1/generate'
```

# response is 403 and body contains `invalid_session_signature`.

jen: They also captured upstream headers (from nginx to our dedicated gateway). Nginx log shows: `Cookie: ACMESESS=eyJ2ZXIiOiIxIiwiZGF0YSI6ImRhdGE...` (full base64) — but our gateway log shows `Cookie: ACMESESS=eyJ2ZXIiOiIxIiwiZGF0YSI6ImRhdGE ` (truncated, trailing space, missing padding `=`). So looks like the value is getting mangled.

vikram: Truncation with trailing space smells like proxy reformatting or a header-size limiting/line-wrapping issue. Nginx by default won't change cookie value bytes, but `proxy_set_header` or some lua plugin might. Also if `proxy_cookie_path` is used, that's for Set-Cookie on responses, not for Cookie on requests. Are they doing `more_set_input_headers` or some `subs_filter`? Ask them for full nginx config for that vhost.

kevin: I pinged the customer for the nginx upstream block. They gave this snippet: 

```nginx
location /app/ {
  proxy_pass http://redwood-dedicated.internal/;
  proxy_cookie_path / /app/;
  proxy_set_header Host $host;
  proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
  proxy_set_header Cookie $http_cookie; # they added this manually for a reason
}
```

sam: Bingo — `proxy_set_header Cookie $http_cookie;` is suspicious because if `$http_cookie` contains characters that nginx tries to re-encode, or if other modules modify header encoding, it can result in truncated/mangled values. Also `proxy_cookie_path` rewrites `Set-Cookie` on responses — not the request cookie — so it shouldn't be needed here.

vikram: Two immediate repro actions for us: (A) capture raw TCP between nginx and our gateway to confirm exact bytes (tcpdump + hexdump of headers), (B) ask them to remove `proxy_set_header Cookie $http_cookie;` and rely on default header forwarding to see if the problem disappears.

jen: I asked them to try removing the `proxy_set_header Cookie` line and to also comment out `proxy_cookie_path` temporarily. They did both on a staging route and confirmed the 403s disappeared and auth passes consistently. They also sent tcpdump where the pre-change stream shows `Cookie: ACMESESS=eyJ...YQ== ` (space at end) and post-change stream shows full base64 with padding `==`.

vikram: That nails it. Explanation: their custom `proxy_set_header Cookie $http_cookie;` causes nginx to reserialize the header value which in their specific config (lua + some filter) led to truncation of trailing `=` padding characters and inserting a trailing space. The signed cookie HMAC covers the full base64 payload, so truncation breaks verification.

sam: Actionable fixes:
- Remove `proxy_set_header Cookie $http_cookie;` (let nginx forward automatically).
- If they need to manipulate cookies, use `proxy_cookie_flags` / `proxy_cookie_path` carefully and test with binary-safe headers.
- As a short-term mitigation on our side, support fallback auth via `X-Redwood-Auth` header that the customer can inject (but we prefer fixing proxy).

kevin: Customer confirmed they removed that line in prod for v1 routes and rolled it out to canary. No further 403 reports in 30m. They're going to audit other ingress vhosts for the same pattern.

vikram: Internal follow-ups for us: (1) add a KB doc describing this exact nginx pitfall (custom Cookie header + lua/plugin edge can truncate `=` padding), (2) add a telemetry check in the Dedicated gateway that warns when incoming Cookie values look short/missing base64 padding for known cookie names (detect truncated base64) and log full request id + hint, (3) add an entry to our onboarding checklist for customers using `proxy_set_header Cookie` (recommend against it).

jen: I'll update the support ticket and paste the repro tcpdump and nginx snippet. Also will create a KB article and link it here.

deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-15T18:12:00Z — canary rollout of support KB changes queued (no infra changes).

vikram: Thanks everyone. Marking this resolved for now but keeping the thread open until KB + small telemetry PR are merged.

jen: tagging follow-ups: sam for telemetry PR, vikram for KB writeup, kevin for customer confirm once they finish audit. :thumbsup:
